name: M*A*S*H
description: Surgeons, soldiers, and survival humor at a mobile army hospital during the Korean War.

episodes.title: Pilot
episodes.premise: Hawkeye and Trapper scheme to raise money for a local boy's college fund by throwing a raffle, setting the tone for how humor masks the horror of wartime surgery.

episodes.title: Chief Surgeon Who?
episodes.premise: Frank Burns protests when the laid-back Hawkeye is named chief surgeon over him, convinced rank should trump skill while wounded pour in from the front.

episodes.title: I Hate a Mystery
episodes.premise: Personal items go missing around camp and Hawkeye plays detective, setting an elaborate dinner-party trap to catch the thief among their own staff.

episodes.title: Dear Dad
episodes.premise: Hawkeye writes a letter home to his father describing Christmas at the 4077th — the pranks, the wounded, and the impossible task of finding holiday spirit in a war zone.

episodes.title: The Army-Navy Game
episodes.premise: An unexploded bomb lands in the compound during the Army-Navy football game broadcast, and Hawkeye and Trapper must defuse it using instructions radioed from HQ.

episodes.title: Major Fred C. Dobbs
episodes.premise: Trapper discovers gold in the hills near camp and the entire unit catches gold fever, abandoning their duties in a frenzy of prospecting and claim-staking.

episodes.title: Dr. Pierce and Mr. Hyde
episodes.premise: Hawkeye goes 72 hours without sleep during a casualty surge and begins hallucinating, refusing to stop operating even as his grip on reality deteriorates.

episodes.title: Deal Me Out
episodes.premise: A marathon poker game in the Swamp gets repeatedly interrupted by crises — a wounded POW, a psychotic patient, and Radar's attempts to play with the big boys.

episodes.title: Tuttle
episodes.premise: Hawkeye invents a fictional officer named Captain Tuttle to funnel supplies to a local orphanage, but the deception spirals when HQ wants to meet their new hero.

episodes.title: Rainbow Bridge
episodes.premise: The 4077th arranges a risky prisoner exchange at a bridge in no-man's land, trading wounded enemy soldiers for captured American GIs under tense ceasefire conditions.

episodes.title: Abyssinia, Henry
episodes.premise: Colonel Henry Blake receives his discharge papers and says emotional goodbyes to everyone at the 4077th, only for devastating news to arrive after his departure.

episodes.title: Welcome to Korea
episodes.premise: BJ Hunnicutt arrives as Trapper's replacement and Hawkeye drives him from Seoul to the 4077th, witnessing the casual brutality of the war firsthand on the journey.

episodes.title: Dear Peggy
episodes.premise: BJ writes to his wife about life at the 4077th while struggling with the guilt of finding moments of happiness so far from home and family.

episodes.title: The Interview
episodes.premise: A TV journalist interviews the staff of the 4077th in black-and-white, and each character reveals their true feelings about the war in unscripted-feeling monologues.

episodes.title: The Abduction of Margaret Houlihan
episodes.premise: Hot Lips vanishes from camp and everyone fears she's been captured by the enemy, launching a frantic search while she's actually on a secret intelligence mission.

episodes.title: Dear Sigmund
episodes.premise: Psychiatrist Sidney Freedman visits the 4077th to treat his own burnout, writing to Freud about the impossible sanity of people living inside insanity.

episodes.title: The Bus
episodes.premise: The staff's bus breaks down in enemy territory on the way back from a medical conference, stranding them overnight with dwindling supplies and rising fear.

episodes.title: Potter's Retirement
episodes.premise: Colonel Potter considers retiring after discovering someone in camp has been filing complaints about him to HQ, shaking his faith in the unit he loves.

episodes.title: Point of View
episodes.premise: The entire episode is shot from the perspective of a wounded soldier who cannot speak, watching the 4077th staff care for him through his own eyes.

episodes.title: Dreams
episodes.premise: Exhausted surgeons collapse for brief naps between waves of casualties and we enter their surreal, disturbing dreams — each revealing deep psychological wounds from the war.

episodes.title: Death Takes a Holiday
episodes.premise: On Christmas Eve, Hawkeye, BJ, and Margaret fight to keep a mortally wounded soldier alive until midnight so his children won't associate Christmas with their father's death.

episodes.title: Old Soldiers
episodes.premise: Potter receives news that the last member of his WWI army buddies has died, and he quietly mourns alone while sharing the story of their decades-long pact.

episodes.title: Heal Thyself
episodes.premise: A visiting surgeon cracks under the pressure of a massive casualty influx, forcing Hawkeye and BJ to recognize how close they all are to the same breaking point.

episodes.title: Goodbye, Farewell and Amen
episodes.premise: The war ends and the 4077th prepares to disband — Hawkeye works through a devastating repressed memory with Sidney while everyone says final goodbyes to the place that changed them.
